text:
morgan: heads up — hit an odd edge case with the auto-fallback rollout today. app A sent a burst of partially-formed requests, runtime flipped to 'silent_degrade', and we fell back to a cheaper model instead of returning errors. billing spiked (more tokens) but user latencies were OK. looking for UX ideas: how should the console show why fallback happened and who can change it?

alex: ugh. can you paste a snippet of the trigger log?

morgan: sure — cropped:
```
[2026-03-20T14:03:12Z] trigger=partial_kvcache_eviction severity=warn route=/v1/generate fallback=silent_degrade reason=kv_eviction_rate>0.3 sample_id=abc123
[2026-03-20T14:03:12Z] decision=auto_fallback selected_model=opt-small cost_delta=+0.003 tokens=210
```

kim: thanks. two UX things pop to mind: (1) surface a short human reason like "KV cache pressure" with a link to the raw log, (2) show expected delta (latency/cost/quality) for the fallback choice inline. both are quick wins. :+1:

praveen: also need RBAC story — who can toggle auto-fallback? currently it's under 'rollout config' which only ops can edit, but marketing teams sometimes request soft fallbacks for experiments. we should show "policy owner" and a changelog entry that links to the rollout id.

elaine: agree on changelog. we should also require an "audit justification" for turning on automatic fallbacks in prod — e.g., a short freeform note and automated checklist (slo impact, fallback validator tests). that way we have context later.

alex: what about replayability? i want a button: "replay decision" that runs the same request through the decision service with recorded signals and shows which rule fired. could be greyed out if the sample is gone.

morgan: replay button would be huge. but privacy/regulatory: some requests are PII — need masking. maybe show synthetic replay (anonymized) and only for users with audit role.

praveen: telemetry: include trigger reason + decision hash + model_variant in trace envelopes. that way dashboards can roll up by reason code (kv_eviction, latency_spike, error_rate). we currently have reason freeform which is hard to aggregate.

kim: agree — make reasons structured enum. UI can then show top 5 reasons and let you filter the rollout timeline by reason.

elaine: UX: in rollout detail panel, add a "why this user saw fallback" flyout that shows: decision reason, event time, cost delta, owner, playback link. and make "auto-enable" toggles show a required confirmation modal that lists potential cost and quality impacts.

morgan: operational question — should automatic fallbacks default to 'monitor-only' on new rollouts? That would avoid immediate cost surprises.

alex: +1. default to monitor, escalate to auto after a canary window (e.g., 24h) and only if no quality regressions. console should show canary window with countdown and a small failures sparkline.

praveen: for RBAC scoping, suggestion: 3 roles — viewer, operator, approver. only approvers can change auto-fallback policy and toggle from monitor->auto. approver actions require an audit note.

kim: misc UX nit: in the alerts panel, show both "fallback activation" and "significant cost delta" as separate alerts to avoid folks missing billing issues.

morgan: sounds like consensus. next steps: small PR to make reasons structured (backend), add the minimal UI chips (reason + cost delta), and an RFC for the RBAC/approver flow. i'll file a short RFC and a small spike for replayability.

elaine: i'll own the RFC for audit/approver flows. will write sample modal copy and investigatory flow.

alex: i'll do the UI spike for the rollout detail flyout and can prototype the replay button.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feat/auto-fallback-telemetry -> staging (sha: f3a1c4b) — running smoke tests. :robot_face:

morgan: thanks all — tagging @eng-sre for visibility on cost alerting.
